deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §12 of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857). That section introduces birational classes of algebraic curves and the count of 3p-3 moduli. The next page carries the count through to 3p-3.

(1) Correspondence of surfaces and change of independent variable. Suppose a rational function z_1 = R(s,z) of the point of the Riemann surface T of F(s,z)=0 is introduced as a new independent variable. Then each point of T corresponds to a point of the surface T_1 spread over the z_1-plane, and conversely. The phrase 'oder die Integrale von Functionen ...' in the top-right insertion widens this to integrals.
- The functions s (and the other rational functions of the system) become functions of z_1 at the corresponding points.
- The integrals of s become integrals of branched algebraic functions of z_1 with the same discontinuities.

(2) Definition of a class (first attempt). All systems of 'gleichverzweigte' functions that can be transformed into one another by such a substitution form one class. A gleichverzweigt system is the field of rational functions on one Riemann surface.

(3) Counts for an m_1-valued function z_1 on a (2p+1)-fold connected surface (genus p), assuming simple branching.
(a) Branch points. As a function of z_1 the system has 2(m_1+p-1) simple branch values. This is Riemann–Hurwitz for an m_1-sheeted cover of the sphere: 2p-2 = -2m_1 + w, so w = 2m_1 + 2p - 2.
(b) Constants. The number of arbitrary constants in such a function z_1 is 2m_1-p+1. My filling, certain from §5 and §12 of the 1857 paper: the functions with m_1 simple poles at given points form an (m_1-p+1)-parameter family (Riemann–Roch, generic case). The m_1 pole positions add m_1 more parameters.
(c) Normalisation. These constants can be chosen so that 2m_1-p+1 of the branch values take arbitrarily prescribed values, provided the branch values are independent functions of the constants.
(d) Implicit conclusion, stated on the next page: 2(m_1+p-1) - (2m_1-p+1) = 3p-3 branch values remain as essential parameters, the moduli.

(4) A started sentence. It reads: 'Faßt man in allen Systemen gleichverzweigter (2p+1)fach zusammenhängender Functionen als unabhängig veränderliche Größe eine solche m_1-werthige Function ein, ...'. That is, use such a normalised function as the independent variable in every system. The sentence is not completed here.

(5) Notation. F(s^n, z^m) denotes a polynomial of degree n in s and m in z. The equation F(s,z)=0 has been transformed by a rational substitution into F_1(s_1,z_1)=0, and conversely.

(6) Definition of a class (algebraic form). Irreducible equations F(s,z)=0 and F_1(s_1,z_1)=0 belong to the same class if two conditions hold together:
- s and z can be replaced by rational functions of s_1 and z_1 so that F=0 goes over into F_1=0;
- s_1 and z_1 are at the same time rational functions of s and z.
This is birational equivalence.

(7) Restatement in function language. If any rational function of s and z is taken as the independent variable, one obtains a system of gleichverzweigte algebraic functions. Classes of equations thus correspond to classes of such systems, which pass into one another by taking a function of the system as the independent variable.
errors: No arithmetic errors. The branch count 2(m_1+p-1) is correct by Riemann–Hurwitz for simple branching. The constant count 2m_1-p+1 is correct, but only generically.

Unstated hypothesis in the constant count: dim L(D) = m_1-p+1 holds for all divisors only when m_1 > 2p-2, and otherwise only for non-special pole divisors. Riemann's 'willkürliche Constanten' count tacitly assumes general position.

The resulting moduli count 3p-3, drawn on the next page, is valid only for p >= 2. For p = 1 it gives 0 instead of 1, and for p = 0 it gives -3, because of continuous automorphisms. The 1857 paper treats these cases separately; this page does not mention them.

The claim that 2m_1-p+1 branch values can be prescribed assumes, explicitly by Riemann, that they are independent functions of the constants. This is a non-degeneracy assumption he does not prove here.

results.what: Number of simple branch points of an m_1-sheeted genus-p Riemann surface over the sphere is 2(m_1+p-1).
A meromorphic function with m_1 simple poles on a genus-p surface depends on 2m_1-p+1 constants.
results.modern_name: Riemann–Roch (Riemann's inequality) plus pole positions; dimension of the Hurwitz space

results.what: Classes of irreducible algebraic equations under mutually rational substitutions; equivalently, function fields viewed with a change of independent variable.
results.modern_name: Birational equivalence of algebraic curves / isomorphism of function fields

results.what: Normalising 2m_1-p+1 branch values leaves 3p-3 parameters (moduli); the conclusion appears on the next page.
results.modern_name: Dimension of the moduli space M_g equals 3g-3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material Riemann published in §12 of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857): birational classes, Riemann–Hurwitz branch count, constant count, and 3p-3 moduli. It is of interest only for showing the drafting process, e.g. the switch from 'systems of functions' to 'irreducible equations'.

checkable.asserts: Branch points minus free constants equals 3p-3 moduli.
Riemann–Hurwitz for an n-sheeted cover of the sphere with simple branching gives w = 2(n+p-1).
A hyperelliptic (2-sheeted) genus-p surface has 2p+2 branch points, consistent with the formula.
The constant count 2m-p+1 equals dim L(D) = m-p+1 plus the m pole positions.
The formula gives -3, 0, 3, 6; correct moduli dimensions are 0, 1, 3, 6, so the formula is valid only for p >= 2.

transcription_corrections: '(2p+1) [?] ... Functionen' should read '(2p+1)fach zusammenhängender Functionen'. 'Functionen als unabhängig veränderliche Größe eine solche m_1 [?] ... Function ein' should read 'eine solche m_1-werthige Function ein' (probable).

In 'die Anzahl der willkürlichen Constanten in einer von s [?] {+Klassen [?]+} ...', the 's' is likely the start of a struck or abbreviated word; the sense is 'in einer m_1-werthigen Function z_1' (cf. next page: 'in der Function z, 2μ-p+1').
'Diese [-...-] {+in z [?]+} lassen sich so bestimmen' reads more plausibly as 'Diese Constanten lassen sich so bestimmen'. The interlinear insertion probably concerns the function z_1.
Line 1, 'nimmt man nun für z als unabhängig veränderliche Größe z_1 auf': the sense is 'nimmt man nun für z als unabhängig veränderliche Größe z_1 an/auf'; the original variable z is replaced by z_1.
'{+s und z+}' above the line 'Zwei durch eine Gleichung verknüpfte veränderliche Größen' is an insertion naming the two variables s and z.
